title: Wild Kingdom & World Tour
description: A lively general-knowledge game covering animal facts, space exploration, fast food history, human anatomy, famous quotes, and world geography.

questions.question: The only bird with nostrils at the tip of its beak, this flightless New Zealand native is also its country's national symbol.
A group of these tall pink wading birds goes by the colorful collective noun 'flamboyance.'
At roughly 22 months, this animal's pregnancy is the longest of any land mammal.
This toothed whale holds its breath for up to 90 minutes while hunting squid at depths exceeding 3,000 feet and has the largest brain of any animal on Earth.
This cephalopod has three hearts, blue copper-based blood, and keeps two-thirds of its roughly 500 million neurons distributed throughout its eight arms.
This U.S. space agency launched Apollo 11 and put the first humans on the Moon in July 1969.
Located just 4.24 light-years from our solar system, this is the closest known star to Earth besides the Sun.
Launched in 1990, this NASA telescope captured iconic images including the 'Pillars of Creation' and the Hubble Deep Field.
questions.answer: What is the Hubble Space Telescope?

questions.question: As of 2025, this ringed planet holds the solar system record with over 274 confirmed moons — far more than second-place Jupiter's 95.
Launched in December 2021, this next-generation observatory orbits 1.5 million kilometers from Earth and detects infrared light from the universe's earliest galaxies.
questions.answer: What is the James Webb Space Telescope?

questions.question: Its golden arches span over 100 countries, and it serves more than 69 million customers every day — more than any other restaurant chain on Earth.
Founded in Columbus, Ohio in 1969, this chain was named after founder Dave Thomas's young daughter and is famous for its square beef patties.
Glen Bell launched this Mexican-inspired chain in Downey, California in 1962, originally selling tacos for 19 cents each.
Fred DeLuca and Peter Buck opened the first location of this sandwich chain in 1965 — DeLuca was just 17 years old, and they started with a $1,000 loan.
Harland Sanders was 62 years old when he began franchising his fried chicken recipe out of Corbin, Kentucky — eventually building this global brand.
Adults have 206 of these, but babies are born with approximately 270 to 300.
Located behind the stomach, this gland produces both insulin to regulate blood sugar and enzymes to aid digestion.
These paired tubes — named after 16th-century Italian anatomist Bartolomeo Eustachi — connect the middle ear to the throat and equalize air pressure.
Pound for pound, this jaw muscle is the strongest in the human body, capable of exerting up to 200 pounds of force on your back teeth.
The only major internal organ capable of regenerating itself after losing up to 75% of its mass — a fact echoed in the myth of Prometheus — is this one.
'To be, or not to be' opens the most famous soliloquy in this Shakespeare play.
'Ask not what your country can do for you — ask what you can do for your country' was delivered by this president at his 1961 inaugural address.
'The only thing we have to fear is fear itself' was declared by this president in his first inaugural address on March 4, 1933.
'I have a dream' was delivered on the steps of this Washington, D.C. memorial during the August 1963 March on Washington.
Historian Laurel Thatcher Ulrich coined this widely quoted phrase — now found on bumper stickers worldwide — in a 1976 scholarly article about Puritan women in New England.
questions.answer: What is 'Well-behaved women seldom make history'?

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef — the world's largest coral reef system — runs along the northeastern coast of this country.
Covering about 6.6 million square miles, this is the world's largest country by land area — nearly double Canada's.
In 2023, this tiny Pacific island nation — with a population of about 11,000 — signed a landmark treaty giving all its citizens the right to live in Australia as rising seas threaten to submerge it.
Covering just 0.44 square kilometers and entirely enclosed within the city of Rome, this is the world's smallest sovereign state.
Completed in 1869, this roughly 120-mile Egyptian waterway links the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, cutting thousands of miles off sea voyages between Europe and Asia.
